prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: Round 1 did not change my view that B044 is the strongest and most mature case before us, and I rest it on the science, not on the fact that all six of us ranked it first. The chain is complete and each link is independently confirmed: proglucagon processing, the truncated active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and effects on appetite and gastric emptying in humans, receptor biology, and then large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Holst (human physiology and secretion), Mojsov (the active peptide) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor actions, translation) each supply a separate, necessary step, and a physiology citation fits the prize's remit. I also hold to a single part. Adding a second part would not improve a case that already stands on its own, and it would use up the three-person cap.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and the exchange did not resolve it. The supplied names do not capture Habener's early proglucagon and GLP-1 work, and the division of credit for the active peptide among Mojsov, Habener and others is disputed in public. I have no primary-record evidence in this file set to settle priority, so I keep Mojsov at full weight only because the supplied credit and the colleagues' statements point to the identification and synthesis of the active form. I would rather state that limit than claim certainty. Excluding Knudsen is a real cost: the physiology is honoured while the people who built durable long-acting drugs are left out. The cap and the discovery framing justify the exclusion. It is not a judgement that her work was minor, and the record should say so.

responses.point: The chair asked whether the B044 citation and laureate set should stay on GLP-1 physiology and the active peptide, or add or substitute a name such as Knudsen for drug development, and which of the three would be dropped under the cap.
responses.response: I keep the discovery framing and do not substitute Knudsen. Every swap damages the chain. Dropping Holst removes the human physiology, dropping Drucker removes the receptor and translational biology, and dropping Mojsov removes the identification of the active form. If the committee wants drug development recognised, that is a different prize and needs more than three seats. The citation should name the active form and the therapeutic consequence in its wording, and the committee record should state that Knudsen's liraglutide and semaglutide work was excluded by the cap and by the discovery framing.

responses.point: Linnarsson raised pairing B044 with a clean basic-mechanism discovery such as B012 as a two-part alternative to a single-achievement prize, given the three-person cap across the union.
responses.response: I considered it and do not support it. The cap is a limit across the whole prize, and B044 uses all three seats, so B012 would need Walter and Mori and a three-person cap would be breached. Cutting B044 to one or two names to make room would remove a necessary step from the strongest case. Walter and Mori are a clean pair, but clean attribution does not make B012 as mature or as consequential as B044, and I would not weaken the GLP-1 trio to fit it. I also still doubt that optogenetics is settled in the way you describe, because its channelrhodopsin discovery and neuronal application are separable achievements.

responses.point: Perlmann asked whether a second prize part is advisable at all, since GLP-1 exhausts the three-person limit and the next candidates each have attribution gaps.
responses.response: I agree, and this moves me from my round-1 openness toward a firmer single-part view. In round 1 I called CAR-T the best second part if one were wanted. After reading the chair's questions I cannot build a defensible second part inside the cap. B018 lacks Eshhar and has an open question over Rosenberg, and B001 has six names for the seats that would remain. I keep B018 and B001 as alternatives in that order only in case the committee decides on a different configuration.

responses.point: El-Manira asked whether a single-part prize is stronger than pairing B044 with CAR-T, and said that the Mojsov credit is contested and he cannot settle it from the files.
responses.response: On the pairing, I think a single part is stronger. The B044 case is complete, and adding CAR-T with Sadelain and June would exceed the cap or force the B044 trio to shrink. On Mojsov, I share your limit: the files do not settle priority. I treat her credit as supported by the identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide, which is separable from Habener's proglucagon work. I would record the dispute and Habener's absence from the supplied names as a limit of the ballot, not as evidence against her.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius favours a three-person physiology prize over a four-person one that adds industrial drug development, and ranks B012 as her first alternative to B018.
responses.response: I agree on keeping the prize at three and on the physiology framing. I differ on alternatives. I keep B018 ahead of B012 because CAR-T has established clinical effect in refractory haematological cancers, whereas the UPR's therapeutic relevance is still developing, and I do not think clean attribution should decide that.

uncertainties: How credit for the active GLP-1 peptide should be divided among Mojsov, Habener, Holst and Drucker, which I cannot settle from the supplied evidence.
Whether leaving out Knudsen and drug development is defensible if the record is read as a prize for the therapy rather than the physiology.
If a different configuration were chosen, whether B018 or B001 has the more defensible set of three or fewer people, given the missing Eshhar credit and the six-name optogenetics field.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict applies to B044, B018 or B001. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and share an institution with colleagues, as I disclosed in round 1, and none of this touches the shortlisted candidates. I do not seek recusal and would flag it if a candidate involving their work arose.
